case.title: TMMS
case.subtitle: Tenant & mall management, end to end.
case.problemBody: A commercial real-estate operator ran a portfolio of malls on spreadsheets and disconnected tools. Tenant onboarding, leases, invoices, monthly sales declarations and maintenance requests each lived somewhere different. They wanted one multi-tenant platform that could be stood up per mall — and infrastructure a small team could actually operate.
case.appBody: A Flutter client tenants use daily: account balances, invoice payment, monthly sales declarations and maintenance tickets — five core workflows in one composed, four-tab app, light and dark.
case.cloudBody: The infrastructure under it: an AWS EKS cluster described entirely in Terraform and Terragrunt, GitOps delivery through ArgoCD, RDS Postgres in Multi-AZ for durability, and Temporal running the workflows that have deadlines — billing cycles, declaration windows, ticket SLAs.
case.outcomeBody: A full infrastructure design and a cost model across three deployment scenarios — single mall, shared multi-mall and isolated enterprise — so spend could be traded against isolation. Releases became GitOps non-events, and the database stopped being a single point of failure.
case.noteBody: Client and figures are under NDA, anonymised here. I’m happy to walk through the architecture and the trade-offs in a call.
